title: Fix a DIN rail to a mounting plate with two loose screws
instruction: Fix the DIN rail to the mounting plate with the two screws: line the rail up so a slot is over each hole, hold it, put a screw through a slot into each hole and tighten both with the hex screwdriver.
context: Building a control cabinet starts with screwing the DIN rails onto the flat mounting plate: the slotted rail is lined up over the plate's tapped holes and held while loose screws are started through its slots and tightened.
setup: All positions from the arm bases' midline (x forward, y left). Fixed on the table: a galvanised steel mounting plate, 300 x 200 x 2 mm on 15 mm folded edges, lengthwise pointing away from the arms, centred 0.25 m forward on the midline, with two tapped M5 holes on its centreline 200 mm apart (0.15 m and 0.35 m forward), each countersunk 90 degrees to 5.5 mm. Loose on the plate: a slotted steel TS35 x 7.5 DIN rail, 250 mm long, 95 g, slots 6.2 x 15 mm every 25 mm along the web's centreline (the first 12.5 mm from the end), lying web-down along the plate, centred on it and turned 3 degrees, both holes under the web between slots. Loose on the table 0.25 m forward and 0.29 m left: a steel screw holder block, 90 x 24 x 30 mm, 0.45 kg, its length pointing away from the arms, with two M5 x 6 hexagon socket head cap screws (zinc-plated steel, head 8.5 mm across and 5 mm high, 4 mm hex socket, 2.7 g) standing head up in collared seats 20 mm apart, and a stubby hex screwdriver (4 mm hexagon blade 10 mm long, 6 mm shaft, red 26 mm handle, 85 mm overall, 35 g) standing blade down in it. A screw catches its thread when it stands upright in a hole and is turned clockwise; about 4 turns later its head is down on the rail, and a quarter turn more tightens it.
scoring: Each screw scores on its own, in either order; the task score is the sum. Per screw: 0.5 if tight (its head down on the rail and turned a quarter turn further; real trial: it doesn't turn further at 2 Nm); else 0.25 if started (in its hole through a slot of the rail, at least 1 full turn into its thread); else 0. A screw only counts through a rail slot (its axis inside a 6.2 x 15 mm slot) with the rail lying flat on the plate (underside within 1 mm of the plate, tilted under 2 degrees). 1.0 (success, ends the run) = both screws tight and still for 1 s.
reset_notes: Unscrew both screws and put them back head up in the holder; put the rail back on the plate, centred and turned 3 degrees with no slot over either hole; put the screwdriver back in the holder.
fidelity: CPU PhysX 240 Hz (-E device=cpu). Own simplified parts, no third-party CAD (rail per EN 60715, screw head per ISO 4762). Thread: a loose screw upright in a hole, turned 20 degrees clockwise, is swapped for a jointed twin (0.8 mm/turn, 0.03 Nm friction, clamp spring); no cross-threading. Tight = 0.25 turn past head contact with 5 N clamp or more, standing in for 2 Nm (real torque and clamp far higher). Rail web and lips 2 mm (real 1 mm); hex key 3.9 mm in a 4.0 mm socket; screw inertia raised.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0; scripted demo: 1.0 (success at step 8,441); one screw tight and one started: 0.75; both started: 0.5; one started: 0.25
